cities.base: Sleep in Penestanan or on the Sanggingan side rather than on Jalan Monkey Forest, which is a traffic sewer from 10:00 to 20:00 and where a scooter passes your window every four seconds. Penestanan is
cities.name: Ubud

cities.base: Sleep at Toya Bungkah on the lake shore inside the caldera, not up on the Penelokan rim where the hotels are built for lunch coaches. From Toya Bungkah the trailhead pickup is ten minutes instead of f
cities.name: Mount Batur and Kintamani

cities.base: Be honest with yourself about what this is. Canggu was rice fields in 2012 and is now continuous three storey construction from Kerobokan to Pererenan, with two roads doing the work of ten and a twent
cities.name: Canggu

cities.base: Stay on the Bingin or Padang Padang side of Jalan Labuan Sait rather than out at Ungasan or Melasti, which are resort compounds with nothing walkable around them. The Bukit is a dry limestone plateau
cities.name: Uluwatu and the Bukit

cities.base: Base in Jemeluk rather than at the Amed village end or out at Bunutan: Jemeluk has the best snorkelling entry, the viewpoint, the freediving schools and enough warungs to eat differently every night,
cities.name: Amed and the east coast

cities.base: There are beds on Penida and staying two nights is the better trip, but almost everyone does it as a day and the arithmetic of that day is brutal: fast boats leave Sanur from about 06:30 and the cross
cities.name: Nusa Penida

places.name: Pasar Umum Ubud before 09:00
places.note: For about three hours it is a working produce market with ceremony offerings, jackfruit and warm jaje bali, and then around 09:00 the same building turns into the souvenir stalls, so the only version worth setting an alarm for is the early one.
places.neighborhood: Jalan Raya Ubud, opposite the palace

places.name: Pura Taman Saraswati
places.note: A lotus pond and a carved gate thirty seconds off the main road, free to walk into, and the reason to come at 08:00 is that by ten the cafe on the left has filled the whole frame with people photographing each other.

places.name: Mandala Suci Wenara Wana, the Monkey Forest
places.note: Around twelve hundred long-tailed macaques and three mossed-over temples in a real ravine forest, which is better than the name suggests; the monkeys take sunglasses, water bottles and phones, entry is IDR 130,000 and last admission is 17:00.
places.neighborhood: Padangtegal, south end of Jalan Monkey Forest

places.name: The Campuhan ridge walk to Karsa Kafe
places.note: Two kilometres of paved spine between two river valleys with elephant grass on both sides, flat and easy, and completely shadeless, so it is a 06:30 walk in April and a mistake at 10:00.

places.name: Museum Puri Lukisan
places.note: The oldest art museum on the island and the one that explains what happened in Ubud in the 1930s, with Pita Maha work and Lempad drawings in four pavilions round a garden; an hour and a quarter here makes every painting you then see for sale on the street legible.

places.name: Tirta Empul
places.note: A tenth century spring where Balinese families still queue at thirty spouts to be cleansed, and where you are welcome to join if you rent the bathing sarong and follow the order of the fountains; entry is IDR 75,000, the coaches land at 10:00, and going in is a different experience from watching fro

places.name: Candi Tebing Gunung Kawi
places.note: Ten shrines cut straight into the rock face of a river gorge in the eleventh century, reached by about three hundred steps down through rice terraces and the same three hundred back up; it is fifteen minutes from Tirta Empul, half the price and a fifth of the people.

places.name: Tegallalang rice terraces at 07:00
places.note: Entry is IDR 25,000 cash and then every farmer whose land the path crosses asks another IDR 10,000 to 20,000, so carry small notes; the terracing genuinely is the old subak system, and the swings, nests and heart-shaped frames that fill it after 09:00 are not.

places.name: The Legong at Puri Saren, 19:30
places.note: Gamelan and a rotating village troupe in the palace forecourt every night at 19:30 for about IDR 100,000, sold from a table at the gate that afternoon; the plastic chairs at the back are a poor seat, so buy by 17:00 and sit in the third row or closer.
places.neighborhood: Ubud Palace courtyard, Jalan Raya Ubud

places.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka 3
places.note: The suckling pig plate that made Ubud's food reputation, and it has been coasting on it for a decade: the lawar and the blood sausage are still good, the crackling is a coin toss after 13:00, and the queue is mostly people who read the same article you did.
places.neighborhood: Jalan Tegal Sari, behind the palace

places.name: Nasi Ayam Kedewatan Ibu Mangku
places.note: Shredded chicken, sate lilit, urap and a chilli sambal that does not negotiate, served on a banana leaf for under fifty thousand rupiah; it is ten minutes out of town, there is no view and no menu, and it is the better lunch by a distance.

places.name: Hujan Locale
places.note: Indonesian cooking taken seriously in an old two-storey house, with sambal matah and a beef rendang that actually tastes of the spice paste rather than of coconut; book a day ahead for the upstairs room, because the ground floor is loud.

places.name: The Mount Batur summit at sunrise
places.note: Seventeen hundred metres, about seven hundred of climbing on loose volcanic scree, and on a July morning six hundred head torches move up it in a single line that stops every few minutes; the view over the caldera and across to Rinjani is real, and so is the fact that you are queuing for it in the d
places.neighborhood: Toya Bungkah trailhead, Pura Jati side

places.name: Pinggan village sunrise viewpoint
places.note: Fog sits in the caldera below you and the cone comes up out of it, which is the photograph most people climb the mountain for; you drive to it, pay a few thousand rupiah for parking, and are back in bed by eight.
places.neighborhood: Pinggan, north rim of the caldera

places.name: The Penelokan rim viewpoint
places.note: The whole caldera, the lake and the 1968 lava field in one frame from the roadside, and the single best five minutes in Kintamani; the terrace restaurants lined up behind it sell a buffet lunch to coach groups that you should walk straight past.

places.name: Pura Ulun Danu Batur
places.note: The second temple of the island's water hierarchy, moved uphill after lava buried the original village in 1926, with eleven-tiered merus and priests who still allocate irrigation water to the subaks downstream; sarong is compulsory and provided.
places.neighborhood: Batur village, rebuilt above the 1926 lava

places.name: Pura Puncak Penulisan
places.note: Three hundred and thirty three steps up to the highest temple in Bali, where the top courtyard holds tenth to fourteenth century stone statues of long-dead royals under corrugated roofing; almost nobody stops, and on a clear morning you see both coasts.
places.neighborhood: Sukawana, the high point of the Kintamani road

places.name: Batur Natural Hot Spring, Toya Bungkah
places.note: Three tiered pools of genuinely hot volcanic water on the edge of the lake, IDR 200,000 at the gate and about IDR 120,000 if you book online first; it is the correct thing to do with your legs after the summit, and the late afternoon is quieter than the post-trek rush at nine.
places.neighborhood: Toya Bungkah, on the lake shore

places.name: The 1968 lava field on the Toya Bungkah road
places.note: Black clinker flows with tomato and chilli plots pushed into the cracks, walkable straight off the lake road with no gate and no guide; the rock cuts, so wear something other than sandals.

places.name: The Songan lake road and the onion terraces
places.note: The last few kilometres of road along the north shore run between the caldera wall and shallot fields worked by hand, with hot springs steaming into the lake at the edge; this is where the Kintamani that is not a viewpoint actually lives.
places.neighborhood: Songan, north end of Lake Batur

places.name: The boat to Trunyan and the open-air cemetery
places.note: The boatmen at Kedisan run a fixed-price cartel, the village asks for a second donation at the landing, and what you have paid twice for is a place where a Bali Aga community leaves its recent dead to decompose under a tree; it is not a sight, and the pressure at both ends leaves everyone unhappy.

places.name: Mujair nyat-nyat at the Toya Bungkah lake warungs
places.note: Tilapia raised in the lake in front of you, fried and then braised in a sweet chilli and shrimp paste sauce, eaten at a plastic table with your feet more or less in the water; order it the moment you sit down, because it takes twenty five minutes.

places.name: A Kintamani coffee tasting on the Penelokan road
places.note: The arabica grown on these slopes alongside citrus is properly good and the free flight of ten cups is a sales funnel; the thing they are steering you towards is kopi luwak, which here almost always means a caged civet, so drink the arabica and decline the rest.

places.name: Batur Global Geopark Museum
places.note: A small government museum that explains the two nested calderas you have been staring at and the 1917, 1926 and 1963 eruptions that shaped the villages; dry, half an hour, and it makes the view mean something. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Pantai Batu Bolong
places.note: Grey volcanic sand, a long forgiving left that is the reason every surf school on the island puts beginners here, and a lineup at 16:00 that is more crowded than the road; swim between the flags because the rip at the rivermouth end is real.
places.neighborhood: Batu Bolong, the main Canggu beach

places.name: Pura Batu Bolong
places.note: A small sea temple on a black outcrop with a walkway out to it, twenty minutes and a sarong, and it is where the sunset actually looks like something rather than at the beach bars on either side.
places.neighborhood: On the rock at the end of Batu Bolong beach

places.name: Echo Beach, Pantai Batu Mejan
places.note: A reef break for people who already surf, a row of bars along the seawall, and the one stretch of Canggu where the sunset crowd still has some locals in it; the sand here is coarse and the water is rarely clear.
places.neighborhood: Echo Beach, north end of Canggu

places.name: The Pererenan rivermouth walk
places.note: Twenty minutes up the beach from Echo puts you past the last of the construction and into rice fields that still come down to the sand; Pererenan is where Canggu was eight years ago and it is being built out at exactly the same speed.

places.name: Tanah Lot at sunset
places.note: A sixteenth century temple on a tidal rock, and the single most photographed silhouette in Indonesia, reached by walking four hundred metres through a purpose-built souvenir arcade with two thousand other people; go at 16:30, look at it from the southern headland rather than the main terrace, and ac

places.name: The Samadi Sunday farmers market
places.note: Sundays only, in a yoga shala courtyard: small growers from Bedugul and Kintamani, raw honey, sourdough and about a dozen food stalls, and it is over by 14:00. This is the one morning in Canggu that rewards getting up.

places.name: Old Man's
places.note: Plastic chairs on grass fifty metres from the sand, cheap large Bintangs, and a Wednesday night that has been the default Canggu night out for a decade; the food is beside the point and the toilets tell you what kind of evening it is.
places.neighborhood: Batu Bolong, at the beach end

places.name: La Brisa
places.note: Built out of reclaimed fishing boats on the sand, with an oyster bar and a minimum spend on the good loungers; it is the least aggressive of the big Canggu beach clubs and you can still sit with a beer and no bottle service.
places.neighborhood: Echo Beach, Jalan Pantai Batu Mejan

places.name: Warung Bu Mi
places.note: Nasi campur from a glass case, pointed at rather than ordered, for around forty thousand rupiah including the ayam betutu; it is the cheapest honest meal within a kilometre of a four dollar flat white and it is always full at one o'clock.

places.name: Crate Cafe
places.note: The big warehouse breakfast that Canggu is known for, decent coffee, enormous portions and a twenty minute wait for a table from 08:30 onward; go at seven or do not go.
places.neighborhood: Jalan Canggu Padang Linjong, Berawa side

places.name: Nook
places.note: An open pavilion with tables looking straight out over a working paddy, Indonesian and western food done competently and cheaply, and the only remaining view of this kind within Canggu that has not been built in front of; it will not last.
places.neighborhood: Umalas, on the rice fields behind Berawa

places.name: Atlas Beach Club
places.note: Marketed as the largest beach club in the world, which is the problem: a car park sized deck for thousands of people, a minimum spend to sit anywhere, and a beach you are separated from by a wall. If you want a day bed and a DJ, La Brisa or Potato Head do it without the scale.

places.name: Pura Luhur Uluwatu
places.note: One of the six directional temples of Bali on a limestone cliff above the Indian Ocean, with a clifftop path north and south of it that is the actual reason to go; entry is IDR 60,000, bring cash, and the resident macaques take glasses and phones off visitors most days of the week.

places.name: The kecak on the Uluwatu cliff, 18:00
places.note: Seventy men chanting the Ramayana in an open amphitheatre with the sun going down behind them, at 18:00 every night for IDR 150,000; tickets often go by 17:00, seats are concrete steps, and it gets cancelled in heavy rain from November to March.

places.name: Suluban Beach, Blue Point
places.note: You go down a narrow staircase between warungs and out through a sea cave onto the sand, and at high tide there is no sand at all, so check the tide table before you walk down; the swimming is poor and the cave itself is the point.
places.neighborhood: Below the Single Fin cliff, Pecatu

places.name: Single Fin
places.note: The best cliff view on the Bukit from a bar stool, straight down onto the Uluwatu lineup, and a Sunday session that has been running so long it is an institution; go on a weekday at 17:00 for the view, or on Sunday if you want the crowd rather than the sunset.

places.name: Bingin Beach
places.note: A short steep staircase down to a reef-fringed cove that is the prettiest sand on the peninsula at low tide; the regency demolished a large number of the cliffside warungs and stays here in 2025 as illegal structures, so what is open changes month to month and you should not count on lunch being the

places.name: Padang Padang Beach, Labuan Sait
places.note: Entry is IDR 15,000 and you reach it by squeezing through a gap in the rocks and down a staircase, which is more fun than the beach, because the beach is about eighty metres long and by eleven there is no space on it; come at 07:30 or go to Thomas instead.
places.neighborhood: Labuan Sait, under the road bridge

places.name: Thomas Beach
places.note: A long white crescent reached by a rough staircase and a dirt track that keeps the coaches away, with two or three warungs renting beanbags; it is the beach the other beaches on the Bukit are usually mistaken for.

places.name: Melasti Beach, Ungasan
places.note: The drive down is a road blasted through a white limestone gorge and it is genuinely worth the trip on its own; the beach itself is flat, swimmable at high tide and now lined with beach clubs, so morning is the only quiet part of the day.
places.neighborhood: Ungasan, down the cut limestone road

places.name: Garuda Wisnu Kencana Cultural Park
places.note: A 121 metre copper statue finished in 2018 standing in a disused limestone quarry, with a paid shuttle, a food court and scheduled dance shows; it is impressive in the way an airport is impressive, and the two hours it costs you are two hours of the Bukit's actual coastline.

places.name: Kedonganan fish market at 06:30
places.note: The boats land between five and seven and the floor is covered in mahi mahi, snapper, prawns and skipjack being cut up on wet concrete; you can buy a fish here and walk it to one of the grill kitchens next door, which is what the seafood dinners on the beach cost a third as much as.

places.name: The Jimbaran beach grills at Muaya
places.note: Tables on the sand under the flight path, grilled fish over coconut husk, and a per-kilo price you must agree before anything goes on the fire, because the printed menus and the actual bill are different documents; the middle row of warungs is cheaper than the two at either end.

places.name: Warung Local Uluwatu
places.note: Nasi campur, ayam betutu and sate lilit at warung prices on the one road everything on the Bukit runs along, with a fan rather than air conditioning; it is where you eat on the days you are not paying resort money for lunch.

places.name: Snorkelling Jemeluk Bay and the underwater temple
places.note: The reef starts about fifteen metres off the black sand and drops away fast, and a set of statues and gates was sunk here at around ten metres as an artificial reef; gear rents for fifty thousand rupiah on the beach and the water is clearest before nine.

places.name: The Japanese shipwreck at Banyuning
places.note: A small steel patrol boat in six to twelve metres of water about thirty metres out, coral-covered and reachable on a breath from the beach, which is why freedivers use it rather than divers; entry is over sharp rock, so bring reef shoes.

places.name: The USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben
places.note: A torpedoed 1942 cargo ship lying parallel to the shore in five to thirty metres, thirty metres off a pebble beach, and one of the easiest famous wrecks in the world to dive; be in the water by 07:00, because from about 09:00 there can be sixty divers on it at once.

places.name: A freediving session with Apneista at Jemeluk
places.note: Amed is one of the two or three places in Asia people come specifically to learn to freedive, because the deep water is a short swim from the sand and there is no current; a two day beginner course runs a few hundred dollars and a single guided session is cheaper.

places.name: The Jemeluk Bay viewpoint
places.note: A lay-by with two warungs looking down on the jukung outriggers pulled up in rows on the black sand; five minutes, a coffee, and it is the picture of Amed that everyone comes back with.
places.neighborhood: On the coast road above Jemeluk

places.name: Sunrise over the Lombok strait from the Amed sand
places.note: Amed faces east, so the sun comes up out of the strait with Rinjani on Lombok in silhouette across the water, and the fishing fleet is coming back in underneath it; no ticket, no crowd, and it is over by 06:45.
places.neighborhood: Any beach between Jemeluk and Lipah

places.name: The Amed salt pans
places.note: A handful of families still make salt here by pouring seawater over black sand, raking it dry and filtering it through hollowed palm trunks, and they will walk you through it for a small fee and sell you a bag; the number of people still doing it drops every year.
places.neighborhood: Banyuning and Purwakerti, along the coast road

places.name: Tirta Gangga water palace
places.note: The last raja of Karangasem's 1946 water garden, rebuilt after Agung erupted on it in 1963, with stepping stones across a carp pond that everyone photographs and tiered pools above that most people miss; entry is about IDR 40,000 and the fish food is a separate small racket.
places.neighborhood: Ababi, 40 minutes south west of Amed

places.name: Taman Sukasada Ujung
places.note: The same royal family's earlier water palace, half-ruined by the 1963 eruption and a 1979 earthquake and rebuilt as an open park with the sea on one side and Agung on the other; quieter than Tirta Gangga and better to walk in.

places.name: Pura Penataran Agung Lempuyang, the Gates of Heaven
places.note: You take a number at the gate and wait between one and three hours for a photograph that a temple employee makes by holding a mirror under his phone, because there is no lake and never was; the temple behind it is a real and important one, and it is not what anyone in that queue is there for.

places.name: The warung strip along the Amed coast road
places.note: Family kitchens strung along four kilometres of coast road doing nasi campur, grilled tuna off the morning boats and sambal matah for well under a hundred thousand rupiah; the cooking is slow because there is one pan, and the tuna is better than anything you will eat in Seminyak for five times the p

places.name: Bali Asli, Gelumpang
places.note: An open wood-fired Balinese kitchen in a field with Agung behind it, cooking a set menu from the village market that morning; it is a forty minute drive from Amed for lunch, they want you to book, and it is the one restaurant in east Bali worth planning a day around.
places.neighborhood: Gelumpang, in the rice fields under Agung

places.name: The Kelingking cliff viewpoint
places.note: A limestone headland shaped like a dinosaur's spine with a white beach at the bottom, and the reason half of Bali's tourists get on the boat; parking is ten thousand rupiah, the viewpoint is free, and between 10:00 and 14:00 there is a queue for the one rock people stand on.

places.name: The Kelingking descent to the beach
places.note: One hundred and fifty six built steps and then two thirds of a very steep dirt path with a bamboo handrail, about a hundred and eighty metres down, twenty minutes on the way down and up to forty back up in heat; swimming has been banned since 2023 after a drowning, so you are climbing down to stand

places.name: Broken Beach, Pasih Uug
places.note: A collapsed sea cave leaving a circular cove with a natural arch to the ocean, and manta rays sometimes visible in the water inside it; you walk the rim in fifteen minutes, there is no shade, and it shares a car park with Angel's Billabong.

places.name: Angel's Billabong
places.note: A clear rock channel that looks like a swimming pool at dead low tide and is a killing chute at anything else; people have been swept out of it and drowned, so look at the tide, and if there is any swell running at all do not climb in.

places.name: Crystal Bay
places.note: The one beach on Penida you can actually swim off, with shade under the trees and warungs behind; the current in the channel past the island is fierce, so stay inside the bay, and every west-loop tour lands here at the same hour for sunset.

places.name: Diamond Beach
places.note: White sand between limestone pinnacles at the bottom of a staircase cut by hand into the cliff, with a rope for the last steep section; entry is IDR 35,000 including parking, swimming is banned because of the rip, and it faces east so it is in shade by early afternoon.

places.name: Atuh Beach
places.note: One hundred and sixty six concrete steps down to a sheltered bay with an arch offshore, warungs on the sand and water calm enough to get into, which Diamond over the headland is not; it takes the sun all day.

places.name: The Thousand Island viewpoint and the Rumah Pohon treehouses
places.note: A cliff edge looking down a line of green sea stacks, with two bamboo treehouses built on the drop that people queue to photograph and a few actually sleep in; ten minutes is enough unless you are waiting for the treehouse shot.

places.name: The Peguyangan blue stairs to Pura Segara Kidul
places.note: A blue-painted steel staircase bolted down a hundred and fifty metres of vertical cliff to a spring-fed temple and rock pools at the bottom, and it is the most genuinely exposed thing on the island; sarong required, no shade, and the climb back up is twenty five hard minutes.

places.name: Goa Giri Putri cave temple
places.note: Fifty steps up, then you crawl through a gap in the rock barely wider than your shoulders and come out in a cavern three hundred metres long with five shrines in it and Balinese families praying; entry is IDR 50,000 with a sarong, and almost no day tour stops here.

places.name: Manta Point off Batu Meling
places.note: Reef mantas circle a cleaning station here most of the year and the sighting rate is genuinely high, but the swell on this coast is exposed and the boat ride makes a lot of people sick; go on the first boat and take something for it beforehand.
places.neighborhood: South west coast, by boat from Toyapakeh

places.name: The warungs above the Kelingking car park
places.note: Mie goreng, nasi goreng, instant coffee and a bench with the cliff in front of it, at roughly double mainland prices; there is nothing else to eat for a good half hour of bad road in either direction, so this is lunch whether you like it or not.

outings.why: Seven hundred metres of loose scree in the dark to a 1,717 metre summit, two hours up and ninety minutes down, with an egg cooked in a steam vent at the top. The hard part is not the climb, it is that around six hundred people do it on a pe
outings.name: The Batur summit at sunrise from Toya Bungkah
outings.season: All year. May to September for a clear summit; from December
outings.fallback: Drive to the Pinggan viewpoint for 05:45 instead and get the caldera under fog for the price of parking, then the hot springs at eight.

outings.why: The two best things in the Pakerisan valley are fifteen minutes apart, so do them as one run: Gunung Kawi first at 08:00 while the gorge is still cool, then the spring at Tirta Empul before the coaches land at ten. Gunung Kawi is three hund
outings.name: Tirta Empul and Gunung Kawi in one morning
outings.season: All year. Avoid full moon and new moon at Tirta Empul unless
outings.fallback: Just Gunung Kawi, and Goa Gajah on the way home.

outings.why: Out along the grass ridge from Pura Gunung Lebah, breakfast at the top, then back down through the paddy paths at Sari Organik into Penestanan rather than retracing the ridge. Six kilometres, no real climb, and entirely without shade, so it
outings.name: The Campuhan ridge and the Sari Organik loop
outings.season: All year. The paddy path section is slick clay after rain.
outings.fallback: The ridge out and back, one hour, and coffee in town.

outings.why: Kelingking, Broken Beach, Angel's Billabong and Crystal Bay, which is what every boat ticket sold in south Bali means by Nusa Penida. It is a 05:15 pickup from Canggu, a 45 minute crossing that is rough from June to August, and four sites r
outings.name: The Kelingking and Crystal Bay west loop on Penida
outings.season: All year. Crossings are cancelled in bad weather, most often
outings.fallback: Stay on the mainland and snorkel Blue Lagoon at Padangbai instead; it is forty minutes from Sanur and nobody drowns in it.

outings.why: The east side is the better half of the island and the worse drive: ninety minutes each way from the harbour on broken road to Diamond, Atuh and the Thousand Island viewpoint, plus Goa Giri Putri on the way back. Far fewer people than the w
outings.name: The Diamond Beach and Atuh east loop on Penida
outings.season: All year, weather permitting on the crossing.
outings.fallback: Do the west loop instead; it is half the driving for the same boat.

outings.why: A 1942 cargo ship torpedoed off Lombok and beached here, now lying thirty metres off a pebble beach in five to thirty metres of water. You walk in from the shore with your tank, which is why it suits new divers, and you have to be in the wa
outings.name: The USAT Liberty at Tulamben, first dive at 07:00
outings.season: All year. Visibility is best April to November.
outings.fallback: Snorkel it instead; the bow sits shallow enough to see clearly from the surface.

outings.why: Deep water twenty metres from the sand, no current and no boat needed, which is the whole reason freedivers come to Amed rather than anywhere else in Indonesia. A guided session or the first day of a course is a morning; the full two day be
outings.name: The Jemeluk Bay freedive session
outings.season: All year. Flat water is most reliable April to October.
outings.fallback: Rent a mask and swim the reef edge off the black sand, which costs about four dollars.

outings.why: Arrive at 16:30, walk the clifftop paths north and south of the temple while there is still light, then the 18:00 kecak in the amphitheatre and out. From Canggu it is ninety minutes each way in evening traffic and a four hour commitment for
outings.name: Uluwatu at sunset and the kecak on the cliff
outings.season: All year. The performance is cancelled in heavy rain, which
outings.fallback: The clifftop walk at 17:00 and a beer at Single Fin, no show.

outings.why: Four beaches on the Bukit, each at the bottom of its own staircase down the limestone, done by scooter between car parks: Bingin, Padang Padang, Thomas, Suluban. The catch is the tide. At high water Suluban has no sand at all and Bingin's r
outings.name: The Bingin to Padang Padang cliff-stair crawl
outings.season: All year. April to October for clean water.
outings.fallback: Thomas Beach alone, which has the most sand at any tide and the fewest people.

outings.why: The boats land at Kedonganan between five and seven and the market floor is at its best around 06:30. Buy a snapper and a kilo of prawns, carry them twenty metres to one of the grill kitchens behind the market, and pay a few dollars to have
outings.name: Jimbaran fish market at dawn, then the Kedonganan grill
outings.fallback: Skip the market and eat the middle row of warungs on Muaya beach at sunset, with the price agreed in writing first.

outings.why: The two Karangasem royal water gardens, forty minutes apart on the road south from Amed, both wrecked by the 1963 eruption of Agung and both rebuilt. Tirta Gangga first for the pools, Ujung second because it takes the late light better and
outings.name: Tirta Gangga and Taman Ujung in an afternoon
outings.season: All year. Both are open and unpleasant in midday sun.
outings.fallback: Tirta Gangga only, an hour, then back for sunset at Jemeluk.

outings.why: Thirty five minutes west along the coast, a temple on a tidal rock, and about two thousand other people. Leave by 16:00, walk out to the southern headland rather than the main terrace where the coaches stop, and expect the car park to take
outings.name: Tanah Lot at sunset from Canggu
outings.season: All year. The rock is cut off at high tide, which changes no
outings.fallback: Pura Batu Bolong at the end of Canggu beach, which is the same idea at a tenth of the scale and five minutes from your room.

outings.why: Thirty minutes east of Ubud, a covered night market that fills at about 18:00 with babi guling, sate, martabak and rujak for a dollar or two a plate, and where the people eating are overwhelmingly Balinese. Go hungry, carry small notes, and
outings.name: The Gianyar night market run from Ubud
outings.fallback: The sate and babi guling stalls on Jalan Suweta in Ubud after dark, which is smaller and thinner but ten minutes away.

outings.name: The Pinggan rim at first light
outings.season: All year. The inversion fog is most reliable in the dry seas
outings.fallback: The Penelokan lay-by, which needs no early start and shows you the same caldera at nine in the morning.

destination.name: Bali
destination.pitch: Ten days split between Ubud, the Batur caldera, the east coast at Amed and one of the two south coasts buys you a genuinely living Hindu culture, the best cheap eating in Southeast Asia and diving off a black sand beach, provided you accept
destination.caveat: Nyepi shuts the entire island for twenty four hours every March, airport included, with nobody allowed onto the street and hotels asking you to stay behind the walls; the rest of the year the tax is the road, where thirty kilometres between Canggu and Ubud can take two hours and any day you plan acr Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Denpasar is a real Indonesian city that almost no visitor uses, and nowhere on the island gives you a walkable urban evening; this is the weakest reason to come.
because.food: Babi guling and lawar in Ubud for four dollars, tuna off the morning boats in Amed, a fish market at Kedonganan you can carry your dinner out of, and one of the most ambitious tasting menus in Asia at Locavore NXT if you want the other end
because.nature: A caldera with a lake in it, a reef you can swim to from the sand at Amed, and cliffs on Nusa Penida that fall a hundred and eighty metres straight into the ocean.
because.culture: Balinese Hinduism is not preserved for visitors, it is the operating system: daily canang offerings, temple anniversaries that empty villages, the subak irrigation councils that still allocate water, and a painting tradition in Ubud you can
because.adventure: A volcano summit before dawn, a shore dive onto a torpedoed freighter, freediving to thirty metres off a beach, and a blue steel staircase down a Penida cliff face.
because.relaxation: Rooms with a private pool for ninety dollars, hot volcanic springs on the lake shore at Toya Bungkah, and a beach culture in the south built entirely around doing nothing for six hours.
because.exploration: Six bases inside a two hour radius that have nothing in common: a volcano rim at 1,500 metres, a fishing coast, a limestone plateau, a river valley of temples and a beach town that did not exist fifteen years ago.
